sections.section_title: Clinical Presentation and Initial Diagnostic Dilemma
sections.description: The clinical narrative begins with a man in his forties presenting to the emergency department with a three-week history of progressively worsening neck swelling and proximal muscle weakness localized to the hip flexors, accompanied by mild myalgia. Despite having no significant past medical history and being a lifelong non-smaker, the prominence of the cervical edema immediately directed attention toward life-threatening surgical emergencies or acute allergic reactions. The initial clinical suspicion favored Ludwig's angina, a rapidly spreading cellulitis of the floor of the mouth and neck spaces, driven by the visible diffuse swelling and inflammation. sections.section_title: Pathophysiology of Anti-SAE1 Dermatomyositis and Non-Histaminergic Edema
sections.description: Idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIM) represent a heterogeneous group of rare autoimmune disorders characterized primarily by chronic muscle inflammation and weakness, often accompanied by distinctive cutaneous manifestations. While the epidemiology shows a bimodal distribution with peaks in childhood (ages 5–14) and adulthood (ages 45–64), the clinical phenotype varies significantly based on the underlying autoantibody profile. Dermatomyositis, distinct from polymyositis and immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy, is defined by a humoral immune response targeting the microvasculature of skeletal muscle. sections.section_title: Diagnostic Reasoning and Multimodal Workup Strategy
sections.description: Once the initial suspicion of infectious deep neck space pathology was ruled out by computed tomography (CT) and the clinical picture failed to align with classic hereditary or acquired angioedema, the diagnostic focus shifted toward identifying an underlying inflammatory etiology capable of mimicking soft tissue edema. The first critical step in this algorithm was the systematic exclusion of primary angioedema mechanisms. Clinicians ordered complement studies, specifically measuring C3, C4, and C1 esterase inhibitor function and quantity.
